description:
A false-colour satellite image displays a landscape featuring a prominent river, agricultural fields, roads, and various water bodies. The river appears in dark blue, while fields and some vegetated areas are rendered in shades of red and magenta. Roads are visible as thin, dark lines.

Two distinct types of water bodies are identified with text annotations and orange arrows:
1.  An orange arrow points to a dark blue water body located near a lighter, exposed bare soil area in the upper middle-right portion of the image. This feature is labelled: "Bare soil = active quarry" and is classified as "8.2.4 Standing water bodies of extractive industrial sites".
2.  A second orange arrow indicates a cluster of interconnected dark blue water bodies in the lower central part of the image, surrounded by red and magenta vegetated areas. This feature is labelled: "Naturalized ponds =" and is classified as "8.2.1 Natural lakes".

The image serves to illustrate the distinction in land cover classification between water bodies within active extractive sites and naturalized or natural lake formations.
